title: ViT-slice: End-to-end Vision Transformer Accelerator with Bit-slice Algorithm
problem: General-purpose processors and existing accelerators inefficiently handle Vision Transformer inference because the primary computational bottleneck lies in linear modules (linear transformation, linear projection, FFN) rather than attention, which has been the traditional focus of acceleration efforts.
motivation: Vision Transformers show strong performance across vision tasks but require specialized hardware acceleration targeting the full computational pipeline to achieve practical efficiency gains.
method: ViT-slice treats numbers as stacks of binary digits and removes the highest-value bits that don't significantly affect the result—this saves computation and storage (bit-slice compression). When multiplying and summing (dot products), it uses learned threshold values to stop the calculation early once the partial result is high enough—a technique called early skip. The accelerator includes specialized circuits: a bit-slice dot product unit (BSDPU) that performs these truncated calculations directly, and integrated compressors that squeeze data moving through the chip.
key_novelty: Bit-slice compression with early-skip computation targets the linear modules—not attention—that are the real bottleneck in Vision Transformer inference, paired with specialized hardware acceleration.
contributions: Bit-slice compression algorithm avoiding redundant MSB storage
Bit-slice dot product with early skip mechanism using trainable thresholds
Specialized bit-slice dot product unit (BSDPU) hardware design
Bit-slice encoder and decoder for on-chip compression

metrics.speedup: 244× over Xeon CPU, 35.3× over EdgeGPU, 16.8× over TITAN Xp GPU, 10.4× over Sanger, 5.0× over ViTCoD

primary_theme: Vision Transformer acceleration with bit-slice compression
